  Code of Ethics

As City of Irwindale Planning Commissioners, our fundamental duty is to serve the public good. We are committed to
the principle of an efficient and professional local government. We will be exemplary in obeying the letter and spirit of
Local, State and Federal laws and City policies affecting the operation of the government and in our private life. We
will be independent and impartial in our judgment and actions.

We will work for the common good of the City of Irwindale community and not for any private or personal interest.
We will endeavor to treat all people with respect and civility. We will commit to observe the highest standards of
morality and integrity, and to faithfully discharge the duties of our office regardless of personal consideration. We
shall refrain from abusive conduct, personal charges or verbal attacks upon the character or motives of others.

We will inform ourselves on public issues, listen attentively to public discussions before the body, and focus on the
business at hand. We will base our decisions on the merit and substance of that business. We will be fair and
equitable in all actions, claims or transactions. We shall not use our official position to influence government decisions
in which we have a financial interest or where we have a personal relationship that could present a conflict of interest,
or create a perception of a conflict of interest.

We shall not take advantage of services or opportunities for personal gain by virtue of our public office that are not
available to the public in general. We shall refrain from accepting gifts, favors or promises of future benefit that might
compromise our independence of judgment or action or give the appearance of being compromised.

We will behave in a manner that does not bring discredit or embarrassment to the City of Irwindale. We will be honest
in thought and deed in both our personal and official lives.

Ultimate responsibility for complying with this Code of Ethics rests with the individual elected official. In addition to
any other penalty as provided by law, violation of this Code of Ethics may be used as a basis for disciplinary action or
censure of a Commissioner.

These things we hereby pledge to do in the interest and purposes for which our government has been established.

REQUEST
Seventh Street Development, Inc., as manager for Alderson BP, LLC, is requesting Site Plan
and Design Review approval for the development of an approximate 42,230 square-foot,
speculative, industrial tilt-up building for property located at 14910 Los Angeles Street.

BACKGROUND/HISTORY
The Irwindale Successor Agency, formerly known as Irwindale Community Redevelopment
Agency, held ownership of both the subject parcel and the adjacent western parcel that has
been developed into Alderson Business Park. Following the dissolution of the redevelopment
agencies in 2012 per Assembly Bill 1484, the Successor Agency prepared the Long-Range
Property Management Plan (LRPMP) to delineate the proposed disposition of each of the
twenty-five properties. Known as Site No. 6 of the LRPMP, 4224 Alderson Avenue/14910 Los
Angeles Street was among the eighteen properties to be sold pursuant to the LRPMP.

On August 26, 2015, the Successor Agency approved a Purchase and Sale Agreement (PSA)
with Seventh Street Development, Inc. authorizing the sale of both parcels with the guarantee
to develop the western parcel into a high-end light industrial business park and to convey
ownership of the subject parcel to the American Veterans. American Veterans Post 113 was
able to purchase the subject parcel in 2015 from the City of Irwindale Successor Agency
through the $2.5 million donation made to the AMVETS California Charities by Seventh Street
Development, Inc.

The subject parcel currently consists of a monitoring well, a paved parking lot, and the La
Ramada American Veterans Post 113 that occupied the subject parcel since 1972, but is
currently unoccupied. The Monitoring Well MW5-01, part of the Monitoring Well Project, was
installed in the eastern portion of the subject parcel in 1991 by the San Gabriel Basin Water
Quality Authority and the US EPA as part of their efforts to identify and mitigate sources of
groundwater contamination in the San Gabriel Valley. The applicant has agreed to provide
an access road to the monitoring well for purposes of monitoring water quality and a condition
of approval has been added to address this.

The subject parcel will change address from 14910 Los Angeles Street to 14988 Los
Angeles Street upon submittal for building permit.

The proposed project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA),

PROJECT DESCRIPTION
Located on 2.3 acres fronting Los Angeles Street, the proposed speculative tilt-up light
industrial building totals ±42,230 square feet with ±37,230 square feet of warehouse space
and ±5,000 square feet of office space. The light industrial building is proposed to be
developed on a speculative basis without pre-commitments from buyers or tenants; however,
Conditions of Approval will be included as part of the project requiring that all users with the
business park comply with the City of Irwindale M-1 (Light Manufacturing) zoning standards
and regulations through the business license and zoning compliance process prior to
occupancy of each use. It is anticipated that the project operations will be conducted during
typical daytime business hours; however, some manufacturers may have evening and night
shifts. All operations will be conducted inside the building per Subsection 17.52.020(B).The
industrial building is to be developed as a “sister building” to the Alderson Business Park
immediately west of the subject site.

Architecture/Design
The proposed tilt-up building will incorporate many of the desired design elements from the
Commercial and Industrial Design Guidelines. The building incorporates multiple
architectural features to break up the expansive exterior walls with architectural projections
and details around the windows. The multi-color palette and arched accent panels,
horseshoe arch with double door, and decorative recessed concrete work together to add
depth and character to the building. The layout, landscaping, and design of the site also
incorporates design elements repeated throughout the adjacent existing Alderson
Business Park (Exhibit C).

E.  PUBLIC WORKS SERVICES

  1. Prior to any trees/landscaping removed by the applicant/developer, the
  applicant shall submit landscape plans for review and approval by the Public
  Works Services Manager.

  2. The owner and/or developer/applicant is responsible for obtaining
  encroachment permit(s) prior to any type of work in the public right-of-way.

  3. Any work within easements on the project site shall require proper permits
  from the easement holder (City of Irwindale, County of Los Angeles, etc.).

  4. The owner/developer shall comply with the National Pollutant Discharge
  Elimination System (NPDES) program and shall require the general contractor
  to implement storm water/urban runoff pollution prevention controls and Best
  Management Practices (BMPs) on all construction sites in accordance with
  the City Code. The owner/developer will also be required to submit a
  Certification for the project and may be required to prepare a Storm Water
  Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP). Projects over five acres in size will be
  required to file a Notice of Intent (NOI) with the California Environmental
  Protection Agency’s State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB). The
  owner/developer can obtain the current application packet by contacting the
  SWRCB, Construction Storm Water Unit, at (866) 563-3107 or by downloading
  the forms from the following website :
  www.waterboards.ca.gov/water_issues/programs/stormwater/construction.shtml.

  The project shall also conform to the City's Ordinance regarding the
  requirements for the submittal of a Standard Urban Storm Water Mitigation
  Plan (“SUSMP”), and the requirements of Low Impact Development ("LID").
  The SUSMP includes a requirement to implement Post Construction BMPs to
  infiltrate the first 3/4" of runoff from all storm events and to control peak-flow
  discharges.

  5. Unless exempted by the Los Angeles Regional Water Quality Control Board,
  a Covenant and Restriction ensuring the provisions of the approved SWPPP
  shall also be required.

  6. No dumping or unpermitted discharges are allowed into the San Gabriel River
  via the Big Dalton Wash.

F.  BUILDING AND SAFETY

  1.  Building permits shall be obtained from the Building and Safety Division and
  all construction shall be in compliance with the Irwindale Building Code and all
  applicable regulations.
